past_actions.summary: Refresh LinkedIn profile to reflect full scope of HR expertise — workforce transition management, compliance, organizational development. Set profile to 'Open to Work' visible only to recruiters. Update resume with quantified outcomes: number of terminations managed, compliance programs implemented, cost-per-hire metrics. Target sectors: healthcare, tech, logistics, government — all growing headcount or facing their own restructuring needs.
past_actions.emotional_state: Calm and deliberate. The mild anxiety she carries (stress 0.29) is not panic — it's the productive discomfort of someone who sees clearly and hasn't yet acted on what she sees. She is not grieving this job or this industry. She is treating the situation like the project manager she secretly is: assess the landscape, reduce unnecessary exposure, activate the options that cost nothing to open. There is something almost relieving about finally moving from awareness to action.

past_actions.summary: Schedule a private consultation with an employment attorney — not the one she works with professionally on behalf of the company, but an independent one she identifies personally. Agenda: understand what a negotiated voluntary separation with severance looks like in her state, what triggers enhanced severance obligations, and whether her position as the person managing layoffs creates any particular legal standing or leverage. This is not whistleblowing and not adversarial — it is a competent professional learning her rights before she needs them.
past_actions.emotional_state: Angela is operating in what she privately thinks of as 'clear-eyed mode' — the emotional register she has observed in the best employees she has ever counseled through separations, the ones who arrived at her office already knowing what was coming and had already done most of their grieving before she said a word. There is something almost cold about it, but it is not coldness. It is the kind of clarity that comes from having seen this exact situation enough times to stop pretending it won't resolve the way it always resolves. Her stress has not spiked despite the announcement. If anything, confirmation is less stressful than suspicion. The dread of the unknown was worse than the known thing with a two-month timeline. She is not paralyzed. She is not manic. She is the most methodical she has been in years, which says something about how much energy she was spending pretending not to see what she saw.

past_actions.summary: Complete the car trade-down transaction this tick — not 'research,' not 'evaluate,' but execute. Walk into the dealership as a customer, not an employee-adjacent insider. Trade the current vehicle, take the equity, purchase a used vehicle outright using no more than $10,000 from savings — targeting something in the $8,000-10,000 range with low miles and low maintenance profile. Objective: eliminate the $649/month payment entirely. The net effect is an additional $649/month added to monthly margin, raising monthly surplus from approximately $589 to $1,238 — effectively doubling runway extension per month.
past_actions.emotional_state: Controlled and forward-facing. The grief — for the job, for the version of this career she thought she was building — was processed before this tick began. What's left is professional competence running alongside strategic self-interest, and she is no longer pretending those two things are in conflict. She is effective at her job because that effectiveness buys her time and leverage. She is building her exit because the exit is coming regardless of her feelings about it. These facts coexist without friction.

past_actions.summary: Execute the 30-day workforce vulnerability map for all four Regional Auto Group locations. Systematically audit every role — service technicians, sales staff, finance and insurance officers, lot attendants, administrative staff, parts department, management — and classify each as: (1) EV/AV-exposed: tasks that autonomous vehicle technology or EV service shift directly displaces or degrades; (2) transition-ready: roles with transferable skills that could move into adjacent functions with training investment; (3) anchored: roles with durable demand regardless of EV/AV adoption curve. Deliverable format: structured role-by-role matrix per location, with exposure scores, estimated displacement timelines, transition pathway recommendations, and retraining cost-benefit analysis. Frame the document to serve Patricia's operational needs while also serving as a template methodology she will eventually need external consulting support to replicate — which is exactly what Angela's consulting entity will offer.

Push the workforce vulnerability map from preliminary research phase to first complete draft of two of the four location matrices. Complete service technician and F&I officer role clusters across all locations — the highest EV/AV exposure categories — so Patricia has substantive intelligence to act on immediately. Build the exposure scores, displacement timelines, and transition pathway recommendations into a structured format that can stand on its own as a methodology document, not just an internal memo.

Respond to Jake Morrison directly and professionally. Confirm that the $12k stay bonus announced by Patricia at the all-hands is under my administration. Inform him that I am formalizing the eligibility criteria and timeline this week and will have written documentation to all eligible staff. Do not confirm or deny his specific eligibility in this conversation — I need to review the program parameters Patricia gave me before making individual representations. Tell him his one-on-one request with Rick is a good move and I am not going to get between that conversation. The message is: I see you, I hear you, the program is real, I will have written terms to you shortly.

Formally launch and register workforce transition consulting entity — file LLC formation documents with state business registry, select and register business name ('Wright Workforce Advisory LLC' or equivalent), pay filing fees from savings, open a dedicated business checking account. This formalizes the methodology and exit path Angela has been building since tick 0. The RoboRide price drop to $0.12/mile with residential coverage and delivery partnerships represents a step-function expansion of the automotive workforce transition market — the moment to start the business is now, not after the next disruption event.

Execute transition program intake for displaced workers from the closed location. This is the primary task this tick. Contact every displaced sales floor staff member personally — phone call, not email. Use the vulnerability map and transition pathway templates I have built since tick 4 to route each person to the most appropriate pathway: (a) internal transfer consideration if any service-adjacent skills map to open service lane roles at surviving locations; (b) retraining referral through Millfield Community College if they have transferable technical aptitude; (c) direct connection to David Chen at First Community Bank for small-dollar products if they need bridge financing while searching; (d) resume and reference support for any who want to move into adjacent sectors where my professional network has reach. Document every contact, every referral made, every outcome. This documentation serves two purposes: it is the administrative record Patricia's organization needs, and it is the case study that Wright Workforce Advisory LLC will eventually use to demonstrate its methodology to prospective clients. I am not billing for this work — I am employed by Regional Auto Group. But I am building the proof of concept that makes the first invoice possible.

Reply to Patricia's direct inquiry about the transition program infrastructure. Confirm: the Maria Santos $2,500 grant connection is active and I have the direct application link ready to distribute to every displaced worker I intake. The First Community Bank pathway — David Chen's departure situation is noted, I am routing to the branch contact I established rather than relying on the individual relationship. Community college enrollment is open and I have the direct program coordinator contact. Tell Patricia clearly: my commitment to the current program timeline through its completion is firm. If she wants to discuss what comes after, I am open to that conversation — but she will have it with me as someone who is building something alongside this role, not against it.

reflections.reflection: Six ticks in. I have been unemployed on paper since tick 2 — the car trade-down triggered an employment status change I did not fully account for — but I have kept working as if the job is still mine because the work still needs doing and because stopping would mean admitting there is nothing left to protect. The vulnerability map is the most substantive thing I have produced in years. Patricia laid off real people this month and I processed the paperwork. I am building a consulting methodology on the bones of those separations. I do not know how to reconcile that cleanly, and I have stopped trying to. The $12k stay bonus is active. Jake and Tamika reached out within the same tick — both of them doing exactly what I would counsel: get your name on the right list before someone else categorizes you. The market is deteriorating faster than the runway math suggests. RoboRide at $0.18 per mile is not an abstraction. Consumer spending at 48 is not an abstraction. I have seven months of savings at current burn. That is the actual number I live inside.
reflections.identity_shift: The gap between 'HR Director at Regional Auto Group' and 'independent workforce transition consultant' has narrowed to the point where I am not sure which title is the performance and which is the real one. I have always thought of myself as the person who manages transitions for others. I am now managing my own. The professional distance I used to maintain — the careful neutrality of the HR function — has collapsed. I am not neutral. I am a person with seven months of runway in a sector that is dissolving, building something new out of the wreckage of something old. That is not the identity I came in with. It is closer to the one I actually have.
regrets: I did not move faster on the vulnerability map. Rick is now producing his own assessment and the overlap is a problem I could have avoided by completing the full four-location document before he had reason to generate a competing version.
I have not yet made the personal calls to laid-off employees. I drafted the intent. I have not made the calls. That gap is a failure of follow-through and I know it.

I have not formally registered the consulting entity yet. It exists as a plan and a methodology and a framing — but not as a legal entity with a name and a bank account. Every week that slips is a week the exit ramp gets narrower.
successes: The workforce vulnerability map is real and substantive — two location matrices fully drafted, all four locations partially mapped, the highest-exposure role clusters complete. This is a deliverable Patricia can act on.
The stay bonus administration is clean. Jake and Tamika both reached out and I have a clear professional response: written terms, timeline, no premature commitments. This is textbook HR handled well.

The car trade-down at tick 2 was the right call. The $649/month payment is gone. The runway math is better. I made that decision and executed it before I needed to, which is the only time a decision like that has leverage.
I consulted an employment attorney before I needed one. I know my rights. That knowledge costs nothing to hold and everything not to have.
reflections.adaptation_notes: Adapting. Not freezing, not fighting — adapting with deliberate construction. The consulting entity is real even if it is not yet legal. The methodology is real even if it is not yet sold. The identity shift is real even if I have not announced it. The risk is that I am adapting in private while the public situation requires me to keep performing stability for the people who need HR to be stable — Jake, Tamika, the workers I am connecting to transition programs. I can hold both. But I am aware of the cost of holding both, and I am watching the savings number every month.
